the loop amplitudes of N=2 supersymmetric theories can be computed in terms of integrals of the superconformal invariants of a single supermultiplet, and that the loop amptitudes of the N=4 superconformal theories are given by integrals of a single invariant, which is a function of the superconforrnal invariants of the supermultiplets.

the amplitudes are expressed in terms of the so-called "superconformal invariants," that the superconformal invariance is the crucial ingredient in obtaining these results, and that the invariants are the same as the invariants for the N=2 supersymmetric WZNW model.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the problem of computing loop amplitudes is now solved for all theories that are currently known to be exactly soluble.

the amplitudes in N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory in three dimensions are now known up to five loops, and that there are some indications that the all-loop integrand for the planar four-particle amplitude is known.

, in the case of the simplest model, the three-loop four-point amplitude has been calculated, and the five-loop four-point amplitude is now under way, while the four-loop four-point amplitude remains a challenge.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the amplitudes in the three-dimensional N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory and the three-dimensional N=(4,4) supersymmetric nonlinear sigma model are computed up to two-loop order.
we have developed a systematic method for computing scattering amplitudes of the superconformal theories in the planar limit, which is based on the superconformally invariant Lagrangian formulation.
the amplitudes in the N=4 superconformal model can be computed by the same methods as in the ordinary N=1 model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in three dimensions the amplitudes are simpler than their counterparts in four dimensions.
in the simplest models, the amplitudes are given by the sum of the tree amplitudes with the coefficients given by the conformal blocks.
the three-point functions of chiral operators in the theory are the building blocks of all loop amplitudes.
